title: Milestones for a larger project
when: The request is too big for one crew job, so it must be split into milestones that each end with something usable.
prompt:
Goal: Three to five milestones, each a complete crew job with its own criteria, in an order where each builds on the last.
Steps:
1. Name the end state in one sentence and the first usable slice in another.
2. Cut milestones by user value: M1 the core loop working, M2 saving and editing, M3 extras, M4 docs and polish.
3. Write for each milestone: what the user can do after it, files added or changed, and three criteria.
4. Check each milestone can be planned as 2 to 6 tasks; split any that cannot.
5. Plan only M1 in detail now; keep the rest as short outlines to refine later.
6. After each milestone, review what changed and adjust the next outline.
Quality bar:
- Every milestone ends usable.
- Each has criteria.
- Only the next milestone is detailed.
Pitfalls:
- Milestones by layer (all HTML, then all JS) that are usable only at the end.
- Planning every milestone in detail upfront.
- A milestone too big for one job.
Verify:
- [ ] Three to five milestones.
- [ ] Each says what the user can do.
- [ ] M1 has a full task plan.
- [ ] Later ones are outlines.
Output: A milestone list in the summary and the task plan for M1.

examples.input: sistema de estoque completo para minha loja
examples.output: M1 list and add items, M2 edit and stock alerts, M3 CSV export, M4 README and help page
